title: Contested Logistics and the "Last Unmanned Mile"
gist: A Cogs of War podcast episode note previews a discussion with executives from Rune Technologies, HavocAI, and CACI on how the U.S. military would sustain a dispersed force under enemy fire in a Pacific war without uncontested access to depots and supply lines, debating autonomy versus automation, predictive resupply, and which logistics lessons from Ukraine transfer to a Pacific theater.

themes.theme: Contested logistics in a Pacific war

insights.claim: In a Pacific war scenario, the U.S. military cannot assume uncontested access to its depots and supply lines for munitions, spare parts, food, water, and energy — a baseline planning assumption the episode treats as unresolved and urgent.
insights.speaker: Tom Garvey, Paul Lwin, David Tuttle, and Jonathan Panter
insights.so_what: Frames contested logistics (not just weapons platforms) as a core capability gap for a Taiwan/Pacific contingency, relevant to defense-tech investment in autonomous resupply, predictive logistics, and sustainment software.

insights.claim: The episode features named executives from three defense-logistics-tech companies — David Tuttle (Rune Technologies), Paul Lwin (HavocAI), and Tom Garvey (CACI) — debating autonomy versus automation and where predictive-resupply data comes from.
insights.speaker: Tom Garvey, Paul Lwin, David Tuttle, and Jonathan Panter
insights.so_what: Identifies three specific companies (Rune Technologies, HavocAI, CACI) positioned in the contested-logistics/autonomous-sustainment defense-tech niche worth tracking for contracts and funding activity.

insights.claim: The discussion debates which logistics lessons from the Ukraine war transfer across theaters to a potential Pacific conflict, implying not all Ukraine-derived sustainment lessons are assumed to generalize.
insights.speaker: Tom Garvey, Paul Lwin, David Tuttle, and Jonathan Panter
insights.so_what: A caution against directly extrapolating Ukraine-war logistics solutions to a maritime/Pacific theater without theater-specific adaptation.

source_meta.author: Tom Garvey, Paul Lwin, David Tuttle, and Jonathan Panter
